claims.summary: For a polynomial matrix A(z) over F_q with H>=1 columns and P parameters, let R count its nonzero rows and form its nonzero-entry row/column support graph. If matching number nu<H, every specialization has kernel dimension>=H-nu. If nu=H, the Cayley polynomial F=sum_j,i y_j w_i A_ji(z), after removing P-Pstar unused parameters, has Newton positive-integral-point weight omega(F)<=R+Pstar. Thus the Adolphson-Sperber certified divisibility exponent beta=(P-Pstar)+omega(F)-R is at most P, so that exponent cannot force a point outside the q^P zero-weight component. No upper bound on the actual valuation or exclusion of coefficient-sensitive/normalized-chart methods is asserted.
